amc8-ajhsme-1997-01.title: Place value
amc8-ajhsme-1997-01.body:
The fractions give the digits in the tenths, hundredths, thousandths and ten-thousandths places: $0.1 + 0.09 + 0.009 + 0.0007 = 0.1997$.

**Answer: (C) 0.1997**

amc8-ajhsme-1997-02.title: Choose the smallest number
amc8-ajhsme-1997-02.body:
To make $200 - n$ as large as possible, choose the smallest two-digit integer, $n = 10$. Then $2(200 - 10) = 380$.

**Answer: (D) 380**

amc8-ajhsme-1997-02.title: Watch out for the trap
amc8-ajhsme-1997-02.body:
$398 = 2(200 - 1)$ would need $n = 1$, which is not two-digit. With $n = 10$: $2 \times 190 = 380$.

**Answer: (D) 380**

amc8-ajhsme-1997-03.title: Line up the digits
amc8-ajhsme-1997-03.body:
Write all with four decimal places: $0.9700$, $0.9790$, $0.9709$, $0.9070$, $0.9089$. The largest is $0.9790$.

**Answer: (B) 0.979**

amc8-ajhsme-1997-03.title: Compare digit by digit
amc8-ajhsme-1997-03.body:
All start with $0.9$. Hundredths digit $7$ beats $0$, leaving $0.97$, $0.979$, $0.9709$. The thousandths digit $9$ in $0.979$ beats $0$ and $0$.

**Answer: (B) 0.979**

amc8-ajhsme-1997-04.title: Find the range
amc8-ajhsme-1997-04.body:
Half an hour is $30$ minutes: $30 \times 150 = 4500$ words. Three quarters of an hour is $45$ minutes: $45 \times 150 = 6750$ words. Only $5650$ is between $4500$ and $6750$.

**Answer: (E) 5650**

amc8-ajhsme-1997-04.title: Convert each choice to minutes
amc8-ajhsme-1997-04.body:
Divide by $150$: $2250 \to 15$, $3000 \to 20$, $4200 \to 28$, $4350 \to 29$, $5650 \to 37\frac23$ minutes. Only the last is between $30$ and $45$ minutes.

**Answer: (E) 5650**

amc8-ajhsme-1997-05.title: Check numbers with digit sum 10
amc8-ajhsme-1997-05.body:
Two-digit numbers with digit sum $10$: $19, 28, 37, 46, 55, 64, 73, 82, 91$. Only $28 = 4 \times 7$ and $91 = 13 \times 7$ are multiples of $7$. $28 + 91 = 119$.

**Answer: (A) 119**

amc8-ajhsme-1997-06.title: Name the places
amc8-ajhsme-1997-06.body:
The $9$ is in the hundreds place ($100$). The $3$ is in the thousandths place ($0.001$). $100 \div 0.001 = 100{,}000$.

**Answer: (C) 100,000**

amc8-ajhsme-1997-06.title: Count the steps
amc8-ajhsme-1997-06.body:
The $3$ is in the $10^{-3}$ place and the $9$ is in the $10^{2}$ place. Going from $10^{-3}$ to $10^{2}$ is $2 - (-3) = 5$ steps, each a factor of $10$: $10^5 = 100{,}000$.

**Answer: (C) 100,000**

amc8-ajhsme-1997-07.title: Side equals diameter
amc8-ajhsme-1997-07.body:
The circle has diameter $8$, so the smallest square around it has side $8$ and area $64$.

**Answer: (D) 64**

amc8-ajhsme-1997-07.title: Avoid the trap
amc8-ajhsme-1997-07.body:
A square of side $4$ (area $16$) is only as wide as the radius, so it can't hold the circle. The square must be at least as wide as the circle: $8 \times 8 = 64$.

**Answer: (D) 64**

amc8-ajhsme-1997-08.title: Subtract school time
amc8-ajhsme-1997-08.body:
From 7:30 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. is $8\frac12$ hours $= 510$ minutes. At school: $6 \times 50 + 30 + 120 = 450$ minutes. On the bus: $510 - 450 = 60$ minutes.

**Answer: (B) 60**

amc8-ajhsme-1997-08.title: Work in hours
amc8-ajhsme-1997-08.body:
School time: $5$ hours of classes $+ \frac12$ hour lunch $+ 2$ hours $= 7\frac12$ hours. He's away from home for $8\frac12$ hours, so $1$ hour $= 60$ minutes is spent on the bus. (Getting up at 6:30 doesn't matter.)

**Answer: (B) 60**

amc8-ajhsme-1997-09.title: Count orders
amc8-ajhsme-1997-09.body:
Three students can line up in $3 \times 2 \times 1 = 6$ orders, all equally likely. Exactly one is alphabetical: $\frac16$.

**Answer: (C) $\frac{1}{6}$**

amc8-ajhsme-1997-09.title: Step by step
amc8-ajhsme-1997-09.body:
The first student must be the alphabetically first one: probability $\frac13$. Then the second must be the earlier of the remaining two: $\frac12$. $\frac13 \times \frac12 = \frac16$.

**Answer: (C) $\frac{1}{6}$**

amc8-ajhsme-1997-10.title: Count unit squares
amc8-ajhsme-1997-10.body:
Make the big square $6 \times 6 = 36$ units. The stripes are L-shapes between squares of sides $6, 5, 4, 3, 2, 1$. Shaded L-shapes: $36 - 25 = 11$, $16 - 9 = 7$, $4 - 1 = 3$. Total shaded $21$: $\frac{21}{36} = \frac{7}{12}$.

**Answer: (C) $\frac{7}{12}$**

amc8-ajhsme-1997-10.title: Odd numbers
amc8-ajhsme-1997-10.body:
The L-shapes from the corner outward have areas $1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11$ (white, black, white, black, white, black). Shaded: $3 + 7 + 11 = 21$ out of $36$, so $\frac{7}{12}$.

**Answer: (C) $\frac{7}{12}$**

amc8-ajhsme-1997-11.title: Work from the inside
amc8-ajhsme-1997-11.body:
$11$ is prime, so $\boxed{11} = 2$. $20$ has divisors $1, 2, 4, 5, 10, 20$, so $\boxed{20} = 6$. Then we need $\boxed{12}$: divisors $1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12$ — six.

**Answer: (A) 6**

amc8-ajhsme-1997-11.title: Divisor formula
amc8-ajhsme-1997-11.body:
For $N = p^a q^b \cdots$, the number of divisors is $(a+1)(b+1)\cdots$. $\boxed{20} = \boxed{2^2 \cdot 5} = 3 \cdot 2 = 6$, $\boxed{11} = 2$, and $\boxed{12} = \boxed{2^2 \cdot 3} = 3 \cdot 2 = 6$.

**Answer: (A) 6**

amc8-ajhsme-1997-12.title: Two triangles
amc8-ajhsme-1997-12.body:
In the big triangle, $\angle 1 = 180^\circ - 70^\circ - 40^\circ = 70^\circ$. Then $\angle 2 = 180^\circ - 70^\circ = 110^\circ$. In the small triangle, $\angle 2 + \angle 3 + \angle 4 = 180^\circ$, so $\angle 3 + \angle 4 = 70^\circ$, and since they're equal, $\angle 4 = 35^\circ$.

**Answer: (D) $35^\circ$**

amc8-ajhsme-1997-12.title: Exterior angle
amc8-ajhsme-1997-12.body:
$\angle 2$ is an exterior angle of the big triangle, so $\angle 2 = 70^\circ + 40^\circ = 110^\circ$. The small triangle's other two angles share the remaining $70^\circ$ equally: $35^\circ$.

**Answer: (D) $35^\circ$**

amc8-ajhsme-1997-13.title: Estimate
amc8-ajhsme-1997-13.body:
The bags are almost the same size, so the answer is close to the plain average $\frac{50 + 25 + 20}{3} \approx 31.7\%$. The $50\%$ bag is the smallest, so the true value is a little lower: $\frac{26}{84} \approx 30.95\%$, closest to $31\%$.

**Answer: (A) $31\%$**

amc8-ajhsme-1997-14.title: Build the set
amc8-ajhsme-1997-14.body:
The sum is $5 \times 5 = 25$. In order $a \le b \le 5 \le d \le e$. The mode $8$ must appear at least twice, and it's bigger than the median, so $d = e = 8$. Then $a + b = 25 - 5 - 8 - 8 = 4$. Since $8$ is the only mode, $a \ne b$, so $a = 1$, $b = 3$. The set is $\{1, 3, 5, 8, 8\}$ and the difference is $8 - 1 = 7$.

**Answer: (D) 7**

amc8-ajhsme-1997-14.title: Check
amc8-ajhsme-1997-14.body:
$\{1, 3, 5, 8, 8\}$: sum $25$ (mean $5$), middle value $5$, and $8$ is the only repeated value. ✓ ($\{2,2,5,8,8\}$ fails because it has two modes.) Difference $7$.

**Answer: (D) 7**

amc8-ajhsme-1997-15.title: Subtract the corner triangles
amc8-ajhsme-1997-15.body:
Let the big square have side $3$ (area $9$). Each corner triangle has legs $1$ and $2$, area $1$. Four triangles: $4$. Inscribed square: $9 - 4 = 5$. Ratio $\frac59$.

**Answer: (B) $\frac{5}{9}$**

amc8-ajhsme-1997-15.title: Pythagorean theorem
amc8-ajhsme-1997-15.body:
The inscribed square's side is the hypotenuse of a $1$-$2$ right triangle: $\sqrt{1^2 + 2^2} = \sqrt5$, so its area is $5$. Ratio $\frac{5}{9}$.

**Answer: (B) $\frac{5}{9}$**

amc8-ajhsme-1997-16.title: Multipliers
amc8-ajhsme-1997-16.body:
$A = 100 \times 1.2 \times 0.8 = 100 \times 0.96$ and $B = 100 \times 0.75 \times 1.25 = 100 \times 0.9375$. Both are below $100 = C$, and $0.9375 < 0.96$.

**Answer: (E) $B<A<C$**

amc8-ajhsme-1997-17.title: Count all segments
amc8-ajhsme-1997-17.body:
$8$ vertices give $\frac{8 \times 7}{2} = 28$ segments. Subtract the $12$ edges: $28 - 12 = 16$ diagonals.

**Answer: (E) 16**

amc8-ajhsme-1997-17.title: Face and space diagonals
amc8-ajhsme-1997-17.body:
Each of the $6$ faces has $2$ diagonals: $12$ face diagonals (like $x$). There are also $4$ diagonals through the inside of the cube (like $y$). Total $12 + 4 = 16$.

**Answer: (E) 16**

amc8-ajhsme-1997-18.title: Price per box
amc8-ajhsme-1997-18.body:
Last week: $5 \div 4 = 1.25$ dollars per box. This week: $4 \div 5 = 0.80$ dollars. Decrease $0.45$, and $\frac{0.45}{1.25} = 0.36 = 36\%$, closest to $35\%$.

**Answer: (B) $35\%$**

amc8-ajhsme-1997-18.title: Ratio
amc8-ajhsme-1997-18.body:
The new price is $\frac{4/5}{5/4} = \frac{16}{25} = 64\%$ of the old price, a decrease of $36\%$. Closest choice: $35\%$.

**Answer: (B) $35\%$**

amc8-ajhsme-1997-19.title: Telescoping
amc8-ajhsme-1997-19.body:
Each numerator cancels the next denominator, leaving $\frac{a}{2}$. So $\frac a2 = 9$, $a = 18$, and $b = a - 1 = 17$. $a + b = 35$.

**Answer: (D) 35**

amc8-ajhsme-1997-19.title: Watch the pattern
amc8-ajhsme-1997-19.body:
$\frac32 = 1.5$, $\frac32\cdot\frac43 = 2$, $\cdot \frac54 = 2.5$, $\cdot\frac65 = 3$: after the factor $\frac{n}{n-1}$ the product is $\frac n2$. To reach $9$ we need $n = 18$, so the last factor is $\frac{18}{17}$. $18 + 17 = 35$.

**Answer: (D) 35**

amc8-ajhsme-1997-20.title: List the products over 36
amc8-ajhsme-1997-20.body:
There are $64$ outcomes. Products over $36$ need both numbers at least $5$:

- $5 \times 8 = 40$ (and $8 \times 5$): $2$
- $6 \times 7 = 42$, $6 \times 8 = 48$ (and reversed): $4$
- $7 \times 7 = 49$: $1$
- $7 \times 8 = 56$ (and reversed): $2$
- $8 \times 8 = 64$: $1$

Total $10$: $\frac{10}{64} = \frac{5}{32}$.

**Answer: (A) $\frac{5}{32}$**

amc8-ajhsme-1997-20.title: Count by the first die
amc8-ajhsme-1997-20.body:
First die $5$: second must be $8$ ($1$ way). $6$: second $7, 8$ ($2$). $7$: second $6, 7, 8$ ($3$). $8$: second $5, 6, 7, 8$ ($4$). First die $1$–$4$: impossible ($4 \times 8 = 32$). Total $1 + 2 + 3 + 4 = 10$, probability $\frac{10}{64} = \frac5{32}$.

**Answer: (A) $\frac{5}{32}$**

amc8-ajhsme-1997-21.title: What changes at a corner
amc8-ajhsme-1997-21.body:
Removing a $1$ cm corner cube takes away $3$ unit squares of surface (its three outside faces) but exposes $3$ new unit squares (the faces where it touched the rest). The surface area doesn't change: it stays $6 \times 9 = 54$ sq cm.

**Answer: (D) 54 sq.cm**

amc8-ajhsme-1997-21.title: Look from each direction
amc8-ajhsme-1997-21.body:
From the front (or any of the $6$ directions), the remaining figure still shows a full $3 \times 3$ outline: the missing corner squares are replaced by the faces of the cubes just behind them. So the surface area is still $6 \times 9 = 54$ sq cm.

**Answer: (D) 54 sq.cm**

amc8-ajhsme-1997-22.title: Compare volumes
amc8-ajhsme-1997-22.body:
Volumes: $2^3 = 8$ and $3^3 = 27$ cubic inches. The value is proportional to the amount of silver: $200 \times \frac{27}{8} = 675$ dollars.

**Answer: (E) 675 dollars**

amc8-ajhsme-1997-22.title: Value per cubic inch
amc8-ajhsme-1997-22.body:
$200 \div 8 = 25$ dollars per cubic inch. $27 \times 25 = 675$ dollars. (The weight is extra information.)

**Answer: (E) 675 dollars**

amc8-ajhsme-1997-23.title: More digits means larger
amc8-ajhsme-1997-23.body:
Digits are different (strictly increasing), so a number with more digits is larger. Try to use as many small squares as possible: $1 + 4 + 9 + 16 = 30$, leaving $20$, not a square. $1 + 4 + 9 = 14$, leaving $36 = 6^2$: digits $1, 2, 3, 6$. Five digits would need at least $1+4+9+16+25 = 55 > 50$, impossible. Other four-digit options: $1 + 4 + 16 = 21$ (leaves $29$), $1 + 9 + 16 = 26$ (leaves $24$), $4 + 9 + 16 = 29$ (leaves $21$), ... none work, so the largest is $1236$. Product $1 \cdot 2 \cdot 3 \cdot 6 = 36$.

**Answer: (C) 36**

amc8-ajhsme-1997-23.title: List all such numbers
amc8-ajhsme-1997-23.body:
Sets of different digits whose squares add to $50$: $\{1, 7\}$ ($1 + 49$), $\{3, 4, 5\}$ ($9 + 16 + 25$), $\{1, 2, 3, 6\}$ ($1 + 4 + 9 + 36$). Written in increasing order: $17$, $345$, $1236$. The largest is $1236$, with digit product $36$.

**Answer: (C) 36**

amc8-ajhsme-1997-24.title: Compute areas
amc8-ajhsme-1997-24.body:
Let $AC = 4$ and $CE = 6$, so the big circle has radius $5$ and area $25\pi$. The upper half of the big circle has area $\frac{25\pi}{2}$. The shaded region is that half, minus the small semicircle $ABC$ (radius $2$, area $2\pi$) that bulges up into it, plus the semicircle $CDE$ (radius $3$, area $\frac{9\pi}{2}$) that bulges down: $\frac{25\pi}{2} - 2\pi + \frac{9\pi}{2} = 15\pi$. The lower region is $25\pi - 15\pi = 10\pi$. Ratio $15 : 10 = 3 : 2$.

**Answer: (C) $3:2$**

amc8-ajhsme-1997-24.title: Compute the lower region directly
amc8-ajhsme-1997-24.body:
Upper $= \frac{25\pi}{2} + \frac{9\pi}{2} - 2\pi = 15\pi$ and lower $= \frac{25\pi}{2} + 2\pi - \frac{9\pi}{2} = 10\pi$ (the lower region gains the $ABC$ semicircle and loses the $CDE$ one). $15 : 10 = 3 : 2$.

**Answer: (C) $3:2$**

amc8-ajhsme-1997-25.title: Group by tens
amc8-ajhsme-1997-25.body:
Only the units digits matter. The numbers end in $2, 4, 6, 8$, and each ten ($2$–$8$, $12$–$18$, …, $92$–$98$) contributes $2 \cdot 4 \cdot 6 \cdot 8 = 384$, which ends in $4$. There are $10$ groups, so the units digit is that of $4^{10}$. Powers of $4$ end in $4, 6, 4, 6, \ldots$; even powers end in $6$.

**Answer: (D) 6**

amc8-ajhsme-1997-25.title: Pair up groups
amc8-ajhsme-1997-25.body:
Each group ends in $4$, and two groups together end in $4 \times 4 = 16 \to 6$. Five pairs: $6^5$ ends in $6$.

**Answer: (D) 6**
